items.statement: Commercial vehicle industry offtake volume expanded by 18.0% year-on-year in Q1, with Tata Motors growing 26%.
items.quote: Q1 saw healthy momentum with offtake TIV growing 18.0% YoY, and TML volumes growing 26% YoY.

items.statement: Diesel consumption grew roughly 2.8% in Q1 FY27, reflecting stable underlying demand.
items.quote: Diesel consumption grew ~2.8% in Q1 FY27, indicating a stable demand trend.

items.statement: E-way bill generation rose 12.4% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, indicating robust domestic trade and goods transport activity.
items.quote: E-way bill generation shows consistent growth of 12.4% in Q1 FY27 over Q1 FY26, signaling resilient goods movement and domestic trade activity during the quarter.

items.statement: Electric vehicle volumes grew 277% year-on-year aided by new product launches and higher diesel prices.
items.quote: With launch of Intra EV, and 55T EV, along with tailwind of higher diesel prices, EV volumes grew 277% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Tata Motors secured orders for 562 units during Q1 FY27 across STU, government, and institutional segments.
items.quote: Won orders for 562 units in Q1 FY27 across government, institutional, and STU segments.

items.statement: The company increased its shareholding in Freight Tiger to approximately 63.6% by acquiring an additional 18.1% stake for Rs 95.66 crore.
items.quote: Freight Tiger is now a subsidiary with the acquisition of an additional ~18.1% equity stake in May 2026 for ₹95.66 Cr bringing its total holding to ~63.6%.

items.statement: The small commercial vehicle range was broadened across fuel types with the launches of Ace Gold+ XL, Intra V40, and Intra EV.
items.quote: Launched Ace Gold+ XL, Intra V40, Intra EV, expanding the SCV portfolio across ICE, CNG and EVs

items.statement: Total investment spending for Q1 FY27 stood at Rs 515 crore in accordance with plan.
items.quote: Investment Spending in Q1 FY27 ₹515 Cr Steady Investments in line with plan

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 23% and EBITDA rose 17% in Q1, reflecting resilient operating margins despite commodity headwinds.
items.quote: Q1: Revenue ₹19.3K Cr(↑23%), EBITDA ₹2.3K Cr(↑17%), PBT(bei) ₹2.1K Cr (↑26%) Resilient margin delivery despite commodity headwinds

items.statement: Tata Motors plans to counter commodity price increases through pricing actions and cost controls.
items.quote: Overall: Manage commodity inflation through price increases and cost management. Address supply chain challenges through targeted debottlenecking in view of increased industry demand.

items.statement: Management plans to fulfill approximately 4,500 orders across STU, defence, and government segments, including 850 electric buses, in Q2.
items.quote: CV Passenger: Execute ~4.5k Government, Defence and STU orders, including 850 e-buses, while sustaining Magic and tender momentum.

items.statement: Tata Motors aims to drive market share growth in SCVPU by leveraging momentum in the Ace and Intra brands and the shift toward EVs.
items.quote: SCVPU: Build on Ace and Intra momentum, leverage shift towards EVs to drive market share gains.

items.statement: The company maintained DEF supplies to navigate supply chain disruptions linked to the Middle East crisis.
items.quote: Uninterrupted DEF supplies ensured overcoming supply chain challenges arising out of Middle East crisis.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Overall: Manage commodity inflation through price increases and cost management. Address supply chain challenges through targeted debottlenecking in view of increased industry demand.

items.statement: Wholesales grew 26% year-on-year to approximately 108,700 units during the quarter.
items.quote: Q1 wholesales were approximately 108,700 units, up 26% year-on-year; a robust quarter and one delivered through a period of heightened geopolitical tensions.

items.statement: Standalone free cash flow turned positive to 1,100 crore rupees, representing a swing of nearly 2,900 crore rupees year-on-year.
items.quote: Free cash flow was ₹1,100 crore, against a negative ₹1,800 crore in Q1 last year. That’s a swing of almost ₹2,900 crore.

items.statement: Standalone profit before tax before exceptional items grew 26% year-on-year to 2,100 crore rupees.
items.quote: EBIT margin was 9.4%, down only 20 basis points and PBT before exceptional items was ₹2,100 crore, up 26% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin contracted by 60 basis points year-on-year due to commodity pressures.
items.quote: EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at a margin of 11.7%, down 60 basis points YoY. The moderation is commodity-led, and I will take you through the walk on the next slide.

items.statement: Commodity inflation in steel, aluminium, and copper drove a 340-basis-point variable cost headwind.
items.quote: Variable costs were the principal headwind at ₹649 crore, or 340 basis points. This is primarily commodity inflation. Steel, aluminium and copper flowing through into material cost

items.statement: Deliveries for the 70,000-unit Indonesia order will take place across FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: And yes, I can only say that the 70,000 orders will certainly be supplied over a period of two years, FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: First-quarter investment spending of 2.7% of revenue fell within the company's guided range of 2% to 4%.
items.quote: Total investment spending in Q1 was ₹515 crore at approximately 2.7% of revenue. This sits comfortably within our guided range of 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Total cost of ownership parity has made electric small commercial vehicles increasingly attractive and supported strong retail demand.
items.quote: SCV pickup, which is completely in the retail market, is in fact doing very well. And as I said, the TCO parity of Intra, Ace Pro has become very attractive in comparison to their ICE brothers.

items.statement: Key logistics indicators such as e-way bills and fuel consumption point to healthy underlying freight demand.
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, Pramod, I think the underlying demand fundamentals are pretty strong, right? We saw e-way bills, diesel consumption, FASTag collection. I think all the indicators indicate very high movement of goods

items.statement: Quarterly price hikes were largely absorbed in the market and contributed 140 basis points to EBIT margin.
items.quote: The price increases that we took during the quarter have largely been passed through and together these added 140 basis points to EBIT margin.

items.statement: The company implemented a 2.5% price increase in July and expects it to pass through during the second quarter.
items.quote: The net price hike in July, we have taken 2.5% increase and very confident that it should pass through as we progress during the quarter.

items.statement: Persistent commodity inflation is being addressed through cost management and price increases.
items.quote: First is the commodity inflation, which continues to be there, which will be managed through first line of attack which is cost management, but we've also taken a price increase on 1st of July.

items.statement: Operating leverage and better realisations offset almost all of the significant commodity margin headwinds.
items.quote: EBIT margin moved from 9.6% to 9.4%. and in summary, operating leverage and improved realisation have absorbed almost all of the significant commodity headwind.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell 90 basis points to 10.9% and EBIT margin fell 80 basis points to 8.5%.
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1 was ₹20,700 crores, up 19% YoY. EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at 10.9%, down 90 basis points. And EBIT was 8.5%, down 80 basis points.

items.statement: First-quarter investment spending stood at 500 crore rupees, in line with company plans.
items.quote: Investment spending was ₹500 crore for the quarter, in line with plan.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing capacity for the Intra EV is sufficient, while battery cell supply from China poses an external bottleneck.
items.quote: In terms of capacity of Intra EV, our in-house capacity is not a challenge at all. What has happened is not only our electric vehicle demand has gone up, which is therefore leading to a cascading increase in demand of cells

items.statement: The company received over 3,400 electric vehicle orders across segments in the first quarter.
items.quote: On Electric vehicles, we strengthened our electric CV leadership with over 3,400 electric vehicle orders across segments, building on the momentum we saw in the second half of last year.

items.statement: The company holds an order book of over 850 electric buses from private operators and state tenders.
items.quote: We also now have around more than 850 electric buses orders. This is a combination of orders from private customers as well as a few tenders that we won from Chennai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, and the state of Odisha.

items.statement: The commercial vehicle passenger business has approximately 4,500 government orders on hand for execution.
items.quote: CV passenger, we still have around 4,500 government orders on hand, which we will continue to deliver during this quarter.

items.statement: Standalone net cash reached 7,100 crore rupees at quarter-end following a 1,473 crore rupee dividend payout.
items.quote: Net cash stood at ₹7,100 crore as of June 30th, against ₹7,500 crore at March-end and this is after the ₹1,473 crore dividend payout during the quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash stood at 13,500 crore rupees as of June 30.
items.quote: And net cash stood at ₹13,500 crore as on June 30, as against ₹13,700 crore at March end, maintaining a strong liquidity position through the quarter.

items.statement: Regulatory approvals for the Iveco transaction have reached the final stage with closing expected in November 2026.
items.quote: On the Iveco transaction - regulatory approvals are now in the final stage, with only one approval pending. All information requests have been addressed, and we expect final clearance by the end of August 2026.

items.statement: The company raised its equity stake in Freight Tiger to approximately 63.6%, making it a subsidiary.
items.quote: On Freight Tiger - we acquired an additional 18.1% equity stake in May 2026 for around ₹96 crore, taking our total holding to approximately 63.6%. Freight Tiger is now a subsidiary.

items.statement: The company introduced the Ace Gold+ XL, Intra V40, and Intra EV to expand its small commercial vehicle pickup line.
items.quote: On the SCV Pick up front, we launched the Ace Gold+ XL, Intra V40 and Intra EV, broadening the SCV PU portfolio across ICE, CNG and electric.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle industry wholesales grew nearly 18% year-on-year in the first quarter.
items.quote: The industry saw healthy momentum with the wholesale volume growing almost 18% on a YoY basis. And our volumes grew by around 26% in the same period.

items.statement: E-way bill generation expanded by 12.4%, signalling healthy freight movement in the market.
items.quote: e-way bill generation shows a very good growth of 12.4%, which does indicate healthy freight available for transportation.

items.statement: Broad-based automotive industry volume growth created supply chain bottlenecks in sheet metal, castings, and forgings.
items.quote: In addition to that, we've also seen some supply chain challenges, especially due to increase in demand in almost all the auto segments, be it two-wheeler, three-wheeler, four-wheeler, commercial vehicles, tractors.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: On EVs, yes, the demand outlook is quite positive. I already gave you the number of orders that we have for the electric buses.
